title: 1 Chronicles 25:9–31
context: The full list of twenty-four lots for the musicians, kept as one unit. Each lot assigns a son of Asaph, Jeduthun, or Heman with his relatives, twelve to a group, for a rotation of service. Several names differ slightly in spelling from the list in 25:2–4.

verses.text: Now the first lot came out for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he and his brothers and sons were twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: “Now the first lot came out for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah.” Arminian readers see the orderly beginning of the rotation, each family receiving its turn without favoritism.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the lot assigning the order of service. Joseph and Gedaliah correspond to names listed in verses 2–3, linking the roster to the families of Asaph and Jeduthun.

verses.text: the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The third lot goes to Zaccur with his sons and brothers, twelve. Arminian readers see each group made up of family members serving together, joined in the work of praise.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the steady pattern of twelve in each group. Zaccur is named among the sons of Asaph in verse 2, so the list follows the families already introduced.

verses.text: the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The fourth lot goes to Izri, twelve. Arminian readers note that the name appears to correspond to Zeri in verse 3, a spelling difference the text leaves unexplained.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise note the likely correspondence while holding it with appropriate caution. Readers in this tradition see the list functioning as a practical roster for temple service.

verses.text: the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The fifth lot goes to Nethaniah, twelve. Arminian readers see another family from Asaph’s line taking its place in the rotation, contributing to the ongoing praise of God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the list’s regularity. Nethaniah is named in verse 2, and the orderly sequence shows that worship was planned rather than left to chance or preference.

verses.text: the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The sixth lot goes to Bukkiah, twelve. Arminian readers see Heman’s family entering the rotation, so that the three founding families share the work.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the lots mixing the families of Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman. Bukkiah heads the list of Heman’s sons in verse 4, linking the roster to the earlier genealogy.

verses.text: the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The seventh lot goes to Jesharelah, twelve. Arminian readers note that this name appears to correspond to Asharelah in verse 2, a variation the text does not explain.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise note the probable identification while acknowledging uncertainty. The variation in spelling does not affect the purpose of the list, which is to record the order of service.

verses.text: the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The eighth lot goes to Jeshaiah, twelve. Arminian readers see another son of Jeduthun named in verse 3 receiving a place, each group contributing its share of praise.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the sequence continuing. Readers in this tradition value the care with which the Chronicler records each family’s role in the worship of God’s house.

verses.text: the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The ninth lot goes to Mattaniah, twelve. Arminian readers see Heman’s son from verse 4 taking his turn, part of a rotation that kept worship continuous throughout the year.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the roster ensuring ongoing service. The orderly pattern reflects a conviction that God is honored by worship that is planned and sustained.

verses.text: the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The tenth lot goes to Shimei, twelve. Arminian readers see another of Jeduthun’s sons named in verse 3 serving with his relatives, reflecting shared family responsibility.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the list moving steadily through the families. Readers in this tradition see in the lists a reminder that ordinary names matter in the service of God.

verses.text: the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The eleventh lot goes to Azarel, twelve. Arminian readers note that the name appears to correspond to Uzziel in verse 4, a difference the text does not explain.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise note the likely correspondence without pressing it. The list keeps its focus on assigning service rather than resolving every variation in names.

verses.text: the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The twelfth lot goes to Hashabiah, twelve. Arminian readers see the first half of the twenty-four groups completed, each receiving a defined place in temple worship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the midpoint of the roster. Hashabiah is named among Jeduthun’s sons in verse 3, and the list continues with the remaining groups.

verses.text: for the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The thirteenth lot goes to Shubael, twelve. Arminian readers note that the name appears to correspond to Shebuel in verse 4, another small spelling variation.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise treat the identification cautiously. The ongoing regular formula shows that every group, whatever its position, held equal responsibility for praise.

verses.text: for the fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The fourteenth lot goes to Mattithiah, twelve. Arminian readers see the last of Jeduthun’s named sons from verse 3 receiving his assignment in the rotation.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the roster’s completeness for Jeduthun’s family. Readers in this tradition note that the lots mingle the families rather than grouping them by father.

verses.text: for the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The fifteenth lot goes to Jeremoth, twelve. Arminian readers note the name appears to correspond to Jerimoth in verse 4, and see Heman’s family continuing in the rotation.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise note the likely identification. The repeated formula underlines that each group was counted and assigned according to the same pattern.

verses.text: for the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The sixteenth lot goes to Hananiah, twelve. Arminian readers see Heman’s son from verse 4 in his place, part of a large family devoted to the LORD’s service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s blessing on Heman’s household reflected in the many groups it supplied. The list quietly displays the fruit of the gift described in verse 5.

verses.text: for the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The seventeenth lot goes to Joshbekashah, twelve. Arminian readers see another of Heman’s sons serving with his relatives, contributing to sustained worship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the steady progression through Heman’s sons. Readers in this tradition note that from here the remaining lots fall almost entirely to Heman’s family.

verses.text: for the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The eighteenth lot goes to Hanani, twelve. Arminian readers see Heman’s family continuing to take up their part in the worship of God’s house.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the lot assigning each group its turn. The regular rhythm of the list mirrors the regular rhythm of service it was designed to organize.

verses.text: for the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The nineteenth lot goes to Mallothi, twelve. Arminian readers see yet another family group from Heman’s line given a place in the ministry of song.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the careful record continuing. Readers in this tradition value the reminder that God’s worship involved many faithful servants whose names are otherwise unknown.

verses.text: for the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The twentieth lot goes to Eliathah, twelve. Arminian readers see Heman’s son from verse 4 taking his assignment as the roster nears completion.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the list drawing toward its close. The orderly pattern shows the Chronicler’s concern that every part of worship be arranged properly.

verses.text: for the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The twenty-first lot goes to Hothir, twelve. Arminian readers see another family receiving its place, part of a system that shared the work broadly among many households.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the roster’s breadth. Readers in this tradition note that the system allowed each group to serve in turn, preventing any one family from bearing the whole load.

verses.text: for the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The twenty-second lot goes to Giddalti, twelve. Arminian readers see the list continuing with Heman’s sons, each group participating fully in the service of praise.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the lot completing the assignments. The repetition of “his sons and his brothers, twelve” emphasizes the uniformity of the arrangement.

verses.text: for the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve;
verses.arminianNotes: The twenty-third lot goes to Mahazioth, twelve. Arminian readers see nearly every family now assigned, with worship organized for continuous service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the roster almost complete. Readers in this tradition see the Chronicler presenting this order as part of David’s preparations for the temple.

verses.text: for the twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
verses.arminianNotes: The twenty-fourth lot goes to Romamti-Ezer, twelve. Arminian readers see the full rotation completed, twenty-four groups ready to lead Israel’s worship.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the total matching the 288 of verse 7. The completed list closes the musicians’ section and shows worship ordered according to David’s plan.
